What We're Reading

Currently Reading

The Midnight Library

by Matt Haig

Fiction · 304 pages · Discussion: Wednesday, January 10th

Nora Seed finds herself in a mysterious library between life and death, where each book allows her to explore a different version of the life she could have lived. This uplifting and thought-provoking novel explores themes of regret, second chances, and the infinite possibilities within each of us.

Why We Chose It

  • Perfect for starting the new year with hopeful themes
  • Engaging and hard to put down
  • Sparks meaningful conversations about life choices
  • Approximately 4–5 hours of reading per week

Past Readings

Lessons in Chemistry

by Bonnie Garmus

Fiction · December 2024

Set in 1960s California, this novel follows Elizabeth Zott, a chemist who becomes a television cooking show host. A powerful story of ambition, perseverance, and breaking through barriers.

Member Highlights

“I loved how the book weaves chemistry and cooking together. Elizabeth is such an inspiring character!”

— Sarah M.

The House in the Cerulean Sea

by TJ Klune

Fantasy · November 2024

A magical and heartwarming tale about a caseworker sent to inspect an orphanage for magical children. Full of humor, charm, and unexpected depth about found family and acceptance.

Member Highlights

“This book made me smile throughout. Perfect for autumn evenings and hot tea.”

— Marcus T.

The Thursday Murder Club

by Richard Osman

Mystery · October 2024

Four unlikely friends in a retirement village form a amateur detective club and stumble upon a real murder case. Witty, charming, and genuinely unpredictable.

Member Highlights

“The characters felt like real friends. Had me laughing out loud and kept me guessing until the end.”

— Jennifer L.

Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow

by Gabrielle Zevin

Fiction · September 2024

An ambitious novel spanning decades and continents, following two brilliant game designers who form an intense creative partnership. Explores friendship, creativity, betrayal, and redemption.

Member Highlights

“A sprawling epic about what it means to create and connect. Complex characters that stay with you long after finishing.”

— David K.

Demon Copperhead

by Barbara Kingsolver

Fiction · August 2024

A modern retelling of Charles Dickens' David Copperfield set in rural Appalachia. A powerful portrait of resilience and the long shadow of trauma and addiction on families and communities.

Member Highlights

“Devastating and beautiful. Kingsolver's prose is stunning, and the story is impossible to forget.”

— Patricia E.

Hamnet

by Maggie O'Farrell

Historical Fiction · July 2024

A haunting reimagining of the life of Anne Shakespeare and the death of her son Hamnet, which inspired Shakespeare's famous tragedy. Lyrical and deeply moving.

Member Highlights

“O'Farrell's prose is like poetry. A beautiful and heartbreaking exploration of grief and genius.”

— Elena R.

Have a Book to Suggest?

Our book selections are chosen by club members! If you'd like to nominate a title for future discussion, we'd love to hear from you. Join us or email us your suggestion.

Home What We're Reading Past Meetings Join Us

Past Meetings

Explore the books we've discussed and the conversations they sparked. Our meetings bring together passionate readers to share perspectives, debate themes, and build lasting friendships through literature.

Meeting Archive

The Midnight Library by Matt Haig

Wednesday, January 10, 2024

Attendance: 12 members

Discussion Highlights:

  • Explored themes of regret and second chances
  • Debated whether the ending was hopeful or bittersweet
  • Members shared personal stories about life-altering decisions
  • Consensus: A feel-good read perfect for January reflection

"This book made me think about the roads not taken, but in a gentle way." — Sarah M.

Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus

Wednesday, December 13, 2023

Attendance: 14 members

Discussion Highlights:

  • Discussed 1960s women's rights and workplace discrimination
  • Praised the protagonist's resilience and ingenuity
  • Enjoyed the blend of science, feminism, and humor
  • Several members interested in learning more about real female scientists

"Elizabeth's journey felt both historical and urgently modern." — James T.

Remarkably Bright by Sophie Kinsella

Wednesday, November 8, 2023

Attendance: 10 members

Discussion Highlights:

  • Analyzed the representation of neurodiversity in fiction
  • Discussed family dynamics and sibling relationships
  • Lighter tone appreciated as a palate cleanser
  • Some members felt the romance subplot overshadowed the main narrative

"A joyful book that celebrates differences and individuality." — Maya K.

The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo by Taylor Jenkins Reid

Wednesday, October 11, 2023

Attendance: 15 members (largest turnout!)

Discussion Highlights:

  • Explored Old Hollywood glamour and behind-the-scenes realities
  • Passionate debate about morality and survival choices
  • Praised the narrative structure and shocking reveals
  • Discussion extended 30 minutes past scheduled end time!

"I couldn't put it down. The twist completely changed how I viewed Evelyn." — David L.

The Thursday Murder Club by Richard Osman

Wednesday, September 13, 2023

Attendance: 11 members

Discussion Highlights:

  • Heartwarming tale of friendship and community
  • Members loved the quirky elderly protagonists
  • Discussed the mystery subplot and plot pacing
  • Universal agreement: need book two immediately!

"These characters felt like friends I never knew I needed." — Patricia G.

Educated by Tara Westover

Wednesday, August 9, 2023

Attendance: 13 members

Discussion Highlights:

  • Moving memoir sparked conversations about family, education, and independence
  • Discussed the impact of isolation on development and worldview
  • Emotional reactions to Tara's journey of self-discovery
  • Several members recommended for book clubs and school curricula

"Raw, honest, and absolutely unforgettable. One of the most powerful books we've read." — Michael R.

We gather every second Wednesday of the month at 7:00 PM. Check back here for upcoming selections and dates.

A cozy spot with coffee, tea, and snacks!

Who Can Join

Everyone is welcome—no experience necessary. Whether you're a lifelong reader or picking up a book for the first time, you'll find a warm community here.

Join Riverside Book Club

Become part of our welcoming community of passionate readers. We meet regularly to discuss literature, share insights, and make new friends.

What We're About

Riverside Book Club is a friendly, inclusive gathering for readers of all levels. Whether you're a seasoned book enthusiast or just looking to explore new titles, you'll find a warm welcome here. We discuss everything from classic literature to contemporary fiction, mystery, memoir, and beyond.

Our members come from all walks of life and bring diverse perspectives to every discussion. No judgment, no pressure—just genuine conversation about the books we love.

Meeting Details

When We Meet

Every second Wednesday

7:00 PM – 9:00 PM

Next meeting: January 8, 2025

Where We Meet

The Bookshelf Café

142 Main Street
Riverside, MA 01234

Comfortable seating, complimentary coffee and tea

Who Can Join

Anyone 18 and older with an interest in reading and discussion.

No membership fees—we're completely free to join.

What to Expect

Lively conversation in a relaxed setting, access to our reading schedule, and a supportive community of fellow book lovers.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to read the book before I attend?

We encourage you to read the selection, but if you're pressed for time or curious about the group, you're welcome to attend and listen. Many members appreciate hearing different takes on the book, and newcomers often find the discussion helpful even if they haven't finished reading.

What if I haven't read much before?

You're in good company! Our book selections range from light reads to challenging works, and we always choose engaging stories. Our group is supportive and patient. We're here to discover books together, not judge reading habits.

Can I bring a friend?

Absolutely! We love welcoming new members. Feel free to bring a friend along. If they decide to join our mailing list, they'll be included in announcements for future meetings and reading selections.

How do you choose which books to read?

Members suggest titles at meetings, and we vote on upcoming selections. We aim for variety—different genres, authors, and reading levels throughout the year. Every voice gets heard in our book choices.

What if I miss a meeting?

No problem. Life happens, and we understand. You'll stay on our mailing list and can attend whenever your schedule allows. We don't track attendance, and there's no penalty for missing a session.

How do I stay updated on the reading schedule?

Once you join, you'll be added to our email list and receive updates about the current selection, discussion dates, and any special events. You can also contact us anytime with questions.

Sign Up Today

Ready to join us? Fill out the form below, and we'll send you details about our next meeting along with the current book selection. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out by phone or email.

Get in Touch

Have questions? Prefer to reach out directly?

Phone: (415) 555-1847

Email: hello@riversidebookclub.local

(415) 555-1847 · hello@riversidebookclub.local
